nodes.label: Chrono Component Discovery Via find_package CONFIG
nodes.rationale: External projects consume Chrono through find_package in CONFIG mode with required and optional COMPONENTS, so a downstream user never names Chrono's internal targets directly. Chrono_DIR can point at either a build tree or an install tree, and the config script exports CHRONO_TARGETS, CHRONO_DATA_DIR, CHRONO_DLL_NAMES and per-component CHRONO_[COMPONENT]_FOUND flags. The script returns early when Chrono_FOUND is false so a missing required module produces a clear message instead of a link failure later.

nodes.label: macOS Application Bundle Requirement For Irrlicht
nodes.rationale: CMAKE_MACOSX_BUNDLE is turned on for APPLE because any Irrlicht-based project must be packaged as an application bundle on macOS to obtain a window server connection; the build output becomes myexe.app and is launched through the contrib/appbundle-macosx run script. For OpenGL-based or non-graphics projects the block is optional and can be removed.

nodes.label: Chrono DLL Copy Command For Windows Runtime
nodes.rationale: add_CHRONO_DLLS_copy_command() copies Chrono and dependency DLLs into the binary output folder so a Windows executable can find them at run time without a PATH change; the call is inert on other platforms, where shared libraries are located through RPATH instead.

edges.source_location: Both resolve optional Chrono modules, but externally via find_package COMPONENTS versus in-tree via CH_ENABLE_MODULE_* guards on the raw targets
